source_standard: Primary sources, foundational papers/monographs, current authoritative standards/guidance, empirical/incident evidence, systematic reviews and serious criticism. Search-result snippets were not used as evidence.
evidence_boundary: Mathematical correctness, standards compliance, tool output and demonstrations are not treated as field-effectiveness evidence unless the operational assumptions and consequence boundary are established.

sources.exact_title: A Statistical Distribution Function of Wide Applicability
sources.claim_supported: Introduces the flexible lifetime distribution later bearing Weibull’s name and shows its use across failure phenomena.
sources.relation_to_property: Life-data modelling, hazard-shape sensitivity, and the rejection of a universal exponential model.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A fitted Weibull form does not by itself identify a physical failure mechanism.

sources.doi_or_publisher_locator: U.S. GPO catalogue locator; Advisory Group on Reliability of Electronic Equipment report
sources.author_or_organisation: U.S. Advisory Group on Reliability of Electronic Equipment
sources.exact_title: Reliability of Military Electronic Equipment
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Full report; especially programme recommendations and testing/prediction sections
sources.claim_supported: Documents the post-war military-electronics reliability programme that joined requirements, prediction, testing, parts control, data and management.
sources.relation_to_property: Historical hardware-reliability lineage and the institutionalisation of reliability engineering.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The catalogue establishes identity and date; specific page claims require consultation of the report copy.

sources.doi_or_publisher_locator: NTNU FMECA teaching chapter citing MIL-P-1629
sources.exact_title: Chapter 3: Failure Mode, Effects and Criticality Analysis
sources.date_version_edition: teaching edition available 2014; historical citation to 9 Nov 1949
sources.claim_supported: Supports the dated historical attribution of the first U.S. military FMECA procedure.
sources.relation_to_property: FMEA/FMECA genealogy only; no effectiveness claim.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The original 1949 document was not directly inspected in this run; attribution is therefore marked historical synthesis rather than primary-text transmission.

sources.exact_title: Procedures for Performing a Failure Mode, Effects and Criticality Analysis
sources.claim_supported: Defines systematic item failure-mode analysis of effects on mission success, performance, maintainability and maintenance requirements.
sources.relation_to_property: Failure-mode/effect propagation, single-point failure identification and FMECA ceremony boundary.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Cancellation and method limitations preclude treating completion of the worksheet as proof that modes are controlled.

sources.author_or_organisation: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission / W. E. Vesely et al.
sources.exact_title: Fault Tree Handbook
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Chs. I–IV; event construction, minimal cut sets, quantification and dependence cautions
sources.claim_supported: Establishes fault-tree analysis as a deductive failure-space model and explains its logical and probabilistic structure.
sources.relation_to_property: Failure propagation, model-boundary discipline and independence-assumption criticism.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A fault tree is complete only relative to its top event, boundary, initiating assumptions and model resolution.

sources.exact_title: Learning Curve Approach to Reliability Monitoring
sources.claim_supported: Introduces the empirical log-log reliability-growth relation later associated with Duane plots.
sources.relation_to_property: Reliability-growth genealogy and the distinction between observed growth trend and causal corrective action.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Trend fit alone does not establish that fixes caused improvement or that future exposure is representative.

sources.doi_or_publisher_locator: Crow report/publisher locator; Reliability and Biometry, SIAM, pp. 379–410
sources.exact_title: Reliability Analysis for Complex, Repairable Systems
sources.claim_supported: Develops the power-law process/Crow-AMSAA treatment for recurrent failures in repairable systems.
sources.relation_to_property: Repairable-system failure intensity and growth modelling.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Inference is conditional on the NHPP/power-law assumptions, data treatment and test-selection process.

sources.author_or_organisation: F. Stanley Nowlan and Howard F. Heap
sources.exact_title: Reliability-Centered Maintenance
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: pp. 21–30 (printed), especially six age-reliability patterns and applicability tests for scheduled work
sources.claim_supported: Shows multiple age-reliability patterns, distinguishes functional from potential failure, and conditions age-based/on-condition maintenance on detectable mechanisms and consequences.
sources.relation_to_property: Maintenance-policy selection, bathtub-curve criticism and P–F interval logic.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Results arose from commercial-aircraft experience and do not imply identical pattern proportions in every domain.

sources.exact_title: Maintainability Prediction
sources.date_version_edition: 24 May 1966; active validation notice dated 26 May 2020
sources.claim_supported: Institutionalises prediction of maintenance-task time and maintainability measures as a design concern distinct from reliability.
sources.relation_to_property: Maintainability lineage, repair-time decomposition and prediction limitations.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Predicted task times do not establish field repairability when access, diagnosis, tools, spares, skills or logistics differ.

sources.exact_title: Failure Reporting, Analysis and Corrective Action System
sources.date_version_edition: 1995 handbook; DLA status page current to 2019 validation
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Purpose, data flow and corrective-action closure requirements
sources.claim_supported: Defines a disciplined closed loop from failure/maintenance data through analysis and corrective action intended to prevent recurrence.
sources.relation_to_property: FRACAS, recurrence control and evidence of effective correction.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A populated database or closed report is not evidence that the causal mechanism was removed.

sources.doi_or_publisher_locator: RAND P-817; reprinted in Automata Studies, 1956, pp. 43–98
sources.exact_title: Probabilistic Logics and the Synthesis of Reliable Organisms from Unreliable Components
sources.claim_supported: Shows mathematically how redundancy and majority constructions can yield reliable computation from unreliable components under stated stochastic assumptions.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The construction’s payoff depends on component-error and independence assumptions that real systems may violate.

sources.exact_title: System Structure for Software Fault Tolerance
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering SE-1(2), pp. 220–232
sources.claim_supported: Introduces recovery blocks and structural separation of acceptance testing, state restoration and alternate implementations.
sources.relation_to_property: Software recovery, containment and fault-tolerant structure.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Acceptance tests and alternate versions can share specification errors or fail to detect semantically wrong results.

sources.exact_title: The N-Version Approach to Fault-Tolerant Software
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 11(12), pp. 1491–1501
sources.claim_supported: Articulates independently developed versions, adjudication and common-mode concerns for design diversity.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Independence is threatened by common specification, algorithm, training, toolchain and interpretation dependencies.

sources.author_or_organisation: John C. Knight and Nancy G. Leveson
sources.exact_title: An Experimental Evaluation of the Assumption of Independence in Multiversion Programming
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 12(1), pp. 96–109; 27 independently produced programs and one million tests
sources.claim_supported: Finds coincident failures significantly above what an independence model would predict.
sources.relation_to_property: Contrary evidence against naïve software-diversity independence.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The experiment’s task and population do not settle every diversity design, but directly refute universal independence.

sources.author_or_organisation: David E. Eckhardt Jr. and Lee D. Lee
sources.exact_title: A Theoretical Basis for the Analysis of Multiversion Software Subject to Coincident Errors
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 11(12), pp. 1511–1517
sources.claim_supported: Provides a theoretical explanation for dependence among independently developed program versions when difficult input regions attract errors.
sources.relation_to_property: Common-mode software failure and limits of diversity.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Theory does not quantify a particular project without an empirical difficulty distribution.

sources.exact_title: Why Do Computers Stop and What Can Be Done About It?
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Failure data and discussion of software, operations, maintenance and repair
sources.claim_supported: Uses field experience to show that software/operations faults and repair processes matter alongside hardware failure.
sources.relation_to_property: High-availability service lineage, repair, operator action and recurrence.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Single-firm operational evidence is mechanism-rich but not automatically transferable.

sources.author_or_organisation: Z. Jelinski and P. B. Moranda
sources.exact_title: Software Reliability Research
sources.claim_supported: Presents an early software reliability growth model based on a decreasing fault content assumption.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The homogeneous fault, perfect-fix and failure-rate assumptions are rarely literally true.

sources.author_or_organisation: Amrit L. Goel and Kazuhira Okumoto
sources.exact_title: Time-Dependent Error-Detection Rate Model for Software Reliability and Other Performance Measures
sources.claim_supported: Develops a nonhomogeneous Poisson software reliability growth model.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A good fit does not prove the latent-fault mechanism or transfer across operational profiles.

sources.exact_title: Operational Profiles in Software-Reliability Engineering
sources.claim_supported: Argues that testing and reliability measurement should reflect the probability distribution of field operations.
sources.relation_to_property: Operational-profile property for software and service reliability.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Profiles age, differ by user class and can omit rare high-consequence operations.

sources.author_or_organisation: Algirdas Avizienis, Jean-Claude Laprie, Brian Randell and Carl Landwehr
sources.exact_title: Basic Concepts and Taxonomy of Dependable and Secure Computing
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing 1(1), pp. 11–33
sources.claim_supported: Separates faults, errors and failures and relates availability, reliability, safety, integrity and maintainability under dependability.
sources.relation_to_property: Failure semantics and plural dependability attributes.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Taxonomy clarifies concepts; it does not by itself establish a system’s achieved dependability.

sources.doi_or_publisher_locator: Methuen Monographs on Applied Probability and Statistics
sources.exact_title: Renewal Theory
sources.claim_supported: Develops renewal processes for repeated events separated by non-negative interarrival times.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Ordinary renewal assumes restoration to an as-good-as-new stochastic state; imperfect repair requires other models.

sources.author_or_organisation: Richard E. Barlow and Frank Proschan
sources.exact_title: Mathematical Theory of Reliability
sources.claim_supported: Systematises life distributions, coherent systems, ageing, maintenance and replacement models.
sources.relation_to_property: Statistical reliability ancestry and model vocabulary.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The authors’ later preface notes that credible system analysis also needs failure-oriented review and attention to mechanical/human modes.

sources.exact_title: Reliability Computation from Reliability Block Diagrams
sources.claim_supported: Defines an RBD as a success-space representation of essential functions required for operation.
sources.relation_to_property: Reliability block diagrams, mission success paths and boundary limits.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: RBD validity depends on correct functional decomposition, state definitions and dependence treatment.

sources.exact_title: Model-Based Fault-Detection and Diagnosis—Status and Applications
sources.claim_supported: Reviews residual generation, detection, isolation and diagnosis using process models.
sources.relation_to_property: Diagnostic coverage, observability and symptom-versus-cause distinctions.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Model mismatch, unmodelled faults and sensor faults limit diagnosis.

sources.author_or_organisation: Andrew K. S. Jardine, Daming Lin and Dragan Banjevic
sources.exact_title: A Review on Machinery Diagnostics and Prognostics Implementing Condition-Based Maintenance
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing 20(7), pp. 1483–1510
sources.claim_supported: Reviews data acquisition, diagnostics and prognostics as components of condition-based maintenance.
sources.relation_to_property: Diagnostics/PHM genealogy and maintenance decision chain.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Sensor data and prognostic output do not ensure useful maintenance unless linked to decisions and validated lead time.

sources.author_or_organisation: Gregory W. Vogl, Brian A. Weiss and Moneer Helu
sources.exact_title: A Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Capabilities and Best Practices for Manufacturing
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Entire review; especially performance assessment and industrial gaps
sources.claim_supported: Synthesises manufacturing PHM capabilities, metrics, data and validation needs.
sources.relation_to_property: Current diagnostics/PHM practice and evidence limits.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Benchmarks and laboratory datasets do not automatically transfer to field production systems.

sources.exact_title: IEEE Standard Framework for Prognostics and Health Management of Electronic Systems
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Framework, data, model and assessment clauses
sources.claim_supported: Provides a common PHM process framework for electronic systems.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Conformance to a framework is not evidence of prognostic accuracy or maintenance payoff.

sources.exact_title: NASA Reliability and Maintainability (R&M) Standard for Spaceflight and Support Systems
sources.claim_supported: Requires objectives-driven R&M planning, explicit failure definitions, analysis of nominal/failed conditions, independent redundancy, test/evidence and restoration capability.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The standard permits tailoring and does not make any single technique sufficient.

sources.author_or_organisation: NASA Office of Safety and Mission Assurance
sources.exact_title: Reliability and Maintainability
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Policy/guidance list, PRA questions and training catalogue
sources.claim_supported: States that R&M concerns performance as required over lifecycle/mission objectives and maintains current guidance resources.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A guidance portal establishes policy and vocabulary, not empirical effect size.

sources.exact_title: Dependability management — Part 1: Managing dependability
sources.claim_supported: Defines dependability as justified confidence in ability to perform as and when required and integrates reliability, maintainability and supportability across life cycles.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Standardisation does not establish that a particular programme achieved field dependability.

sources.exact_title: Dependability management — Part 3-10: Application guide — Maintainability and maintenance
sources.claim_supported: Treats maintainability and maintenance across hardware, software, services and structures and their lifecycle interfaces.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Application remains context-dependent and requires field-resource validation.

sources.exact_title: Dependability management — Part 3-14: Application guide — Supportability and support
sources.claim_supported: Makes supportability, support resources and lifecycle planning explicit contributors to availability.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A maintainable item can remain unavailable when support resources are absent.

sources.exact_title: Dependability management — Part 3-2: Application guide — Collection of dependability data from the field
sources.claim_supported: Specifies collection of field dependability data with context necessary for feedback and estimation.
sources.relation_to_property: Field calibration, exposure denominator and configuration binding.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Field-return databases can be biased by reporting, censoring and population changes.

sources.exact_title: Dependability management — Part 3-11: Application guide — Reliability centred maintenance
sources.claim_supported: Provides an RCM application framework relating functions, functional failures, consequences and maintenance tasks.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: RCM paperwork is not a substitute for valid failure mechanisms or task-effectiveness evidence.

sources.exact_title: Failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA and FMECA)
sources.claim_supported: Provides current consensus procedures for FMEA/FMECA and recognises tailoring to objectives.
sources.relation_to_property: Failure-analysis lineage and evolved method form.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Ordinal scoring and worksheet completeness remain vulnerable to subjectivity and omissions.

sources.exact_title: Mathematical expressions for reliability, availability, maintainability and maintenance support terms
sources.claim_supported: Separates and mathematically defines reliability, availability, maintainability and support measures for repairable and non-repairable items.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Formula validity remains conditional on item class, stochastic model and state definition.

sources.exact_title: Methods for Product Accelerated Testing
sources.claim_supported: Covers accelerated reliability testing and model-based interpretation.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Acceleration that activates a different failure mechanism cannot establish field life.

sources.author_or_organisation: U.S. Department of Defense, Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering
sources.exact_title: Reliability and Maintainability Engineering
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Mission, logistics, design-influence and required activity list
sources.claim_supported: Frames R&M as design influence for mission capability, availability and logistics burden and requires failure definitions, FMECA, testing, demonstrations and FRACAS.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The activity list is not itself proof that the activities are decision-effective.

sources.exact_title: Electronic Reliability Design Handbook
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Definitions, design analysis, test and prediction chapters
sources.claim_supported: Shows continued official use of a broad electronic-reliability design handbook in 2026.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Continued validation does not override documented criticism of handbook-style field-rate prediction.

sources.doi_or_publisher_locator: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, reliability chapter
sources.exact_title: Assessing Product Reliability
sources.claim_supported: Provides life-data, repairable-system, test-planning, acceleration and uncertainty methods with explicit assumptions.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Examples are methodological; representativeness and failure-mechanism validity remain engineering questions.

sources.exact_title: Bathtub Curve
sources.claim_supported: Explains the three-part bathtub idealisation and its component hazard regions.
sources.relation_to_property: Bathtub-curve model, not universal empirical law.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Observed products may not pass through all three phases and mixtures can produce misleading aggregate shapes.

sources.exact_title: How Do You Select the Best Reliability Model?
sources.claim_supported: Warns that multiple distributions can fit small data sets yet extrapolate very differently; engineering knowledge must guide selection.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Goodness-of-fit alone is weak evidence for tail prediction.

sources.exact_title: Exponential Life Distribution (or HPP Model) Tests
sources.claim_supported: Makes explicit that MTBF testing under the exponential/HPP model assumes constant failure or repair rate.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Using MTBF outside that model hides age, mixture and recurrent-event structure.

sources.exact_title: Constant Repair Rate (HPP/Exponential) Model
sources.claim_supported: Describes HPP repairable-system MTBF estimation and confidence bounds.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Convenience and tractable confidence intervals do not establish constant intensity.

sources.exact_title: Acceleration Models
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Accelerated life model and validation sections
sources.claim_supported: Requires an acceleration relationship appropriate to the active failure mechanism and recommends model validation.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Extrapolation can be grossly wrong when stress changes mechanism or model form.

sources.author_or_organisation: Georgia A. Klutke, Peter C. Kiessler and Mark A. Wortman
sources.exact_title: A Critical Look at the Bathtub Curve
sources.claim_supported: Critiques routine assumption of the bathtub curve and examines conditions producing it.
sources.relation_to_property: Contrary evidence to universal bathtub claims.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: It criticises overgeneralisation, not all uses of piecewise hazard reasoning.

sources.author_or_organisation: National Research Council; Anto Peter, Diganta Das and Michael Pecht
sources.exact_title: Critique of MIL-HDBK-217
sources.claim_supported: Documents outdated data, constant-rate assumptions, missing mechanisms and large prediction errors in MIL-HDBK-217-type methods.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The critique does not imply that all comparative prediction or physics-informed modelling is valueless.

sources.exact_title: Reliability Growth: Enhancing Defense System Reliability
sources.claim_supported: Reviews defence reliability-growth planning, testing, models, management and evidence limitations.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Growth programmes can fail through insufficient test time, unrepresentative exposure, delayed fixes and weak management closure.

sources.author_or_organisation: Martin Dazer, Alexander Grundler, Philipp Mell, Achim Benz and Marco Arndt
sources.exact_title: Risk Based Reliability Demonstration Test Planning for Decision Making Under Uncertainty
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: PSAM 16 paper DA21, especially abstract, §1 and the success-run/zero-failure discussion on pp. 1–5
sources.claim_supported: Shows that reliability-demonstration evidence and test-planning decisions remain conditional on confidence, test strategy, prior knowledge and type-I/type-II error; success-run evidence does not identify the lifetime distribution.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: No observed failures does not imply zero failure probability or identify a failure distribution.

sources.exact_title: Binomial Reliability Demonstration Tests with Dependent Data
sources.claim_supported: Examines binomial reliability demonstration when observations are dependent and derives sample-size implications under a Markov dependence model.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Classical binomial results can overstate evidence when units or trials are correlated.

sources.exact_title: On the Statistical Modeling and Analysis of Repairable Systems
sources.claim_supported: Reviews renewal, HPP, NHPP and trend/repairable-system models and their interpretation.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Treating recurrent failures as independent component lifetimes can misstate trend and repair effects.

sources.author_or_organisation: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission / Idaho National Laboratory
sources.exact_title: Common-Cause Failure Database and Analysis System: Event Data Collection, Classification, and Coding
sources.claim_supported: Defines empirical criteria for common-cause events, shared causes and coupling factors.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Database classification has reporting and domain boundaries; beta factors are not universal constants.

sources.author_or_organisation: NASA Scientific and Technical Information Program
sources.exact_title: Fault Tree Analysis
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: NASA/SP-2000-6111, introductory overview and indexed bibliography
sources.claim_supported: Characterises fault-tree analysis as a top-down method and documents the aerospace/process-hazard literature available through NASA STI at publication.
sources.relation_to_property: FTA genealogy and method cross-domain use.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A bibliography and overview do not establish completeness, numerical validity or effectiveness for a particular system.

sources.exact_title: Common Cause Failures Dominate and Defeat Redundancy
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: 2025 Annual Reliability and Maintainability Symposium paper; NTRS record and complete paper
sources.claim_supported: Argues from reliability examples that specification, design, manufacturing, operation and maintenance common causes can dominate nominal redundancy benefits.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Illustrative analyses should not be treated as universal quantitative frequencies.

sources.author_or_organisation: Jose E. Ramirez-Marquez and David W. Coit
sources.exact_title: Optimization of System Reliability in the Presence of Common Cause Failures
sources.claim_supported: Shows that accounting for common-cause failures changes redundancy-allocation optimisation.
sources.relation_to_property: Formal support for explicit CCF modelling.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Optimisation remains conditional on model structure and parameter estimates.

sources.exact_title: Guide for Cybersecurity Event Recovery
sources.claim_supported: Treats recovery as a gradient involving people, process and technology; requires realistic exercises, data-integrity validation, staging and acceptance criteria.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Cybersecurity context supplies a boundary case; reliability claims should import only recovery mechanisms, not security conclusions.

sources.author_or_organisation: Toby Maysey, Michael Powell, Jake Steel and Stephanie Sarvia, National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.exact_title: OT Backup Quick Start Guide
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: pp. 1–2, especially “Backup Integrity Testing and Restoration”
sources.claim_supported: Requires recurring restore tests on non-production systems, backup-integrity checks, restoration practice, documentation and verification of restored functional integrity.
sources.relation_to_property: Tested backup/restore property and current frontier.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: OT-specific implementation details are domain-specific.

sources.exact_title: Summary of the Amazon S3 Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Paras. describing capacity-removal command, dependency impact, slow full restart and safeguards
sources.claim_supported: Shows human-tool interaction, shared dependency blast radius, untested-at-scale restart and recovery-time surprises.
sources.relation_to_property: Field support for containment, dependency mapping, safeguards and current recovery tests.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Provider-authored postmortem may omit information, but mechanism detail is directly relevant.

sources.exact_title: More Details About the October 4 Outage
sources.claim_supported: Shows correlated backbone, DNS, tool-access and physical-access dependencies; recovery required staged load return.
sources.relation_to_property: Dependency/correlation, observability during failure and reconstitution.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Provider-authored account is not an independent investigation.

sources.exact_title: Postmortem of Database Outage of January 31
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Data-loss impact, backup/replication and restore root-cause sections
sources.claim_supported: Shows that nominal standby and backups can be unavailable, stale or untested and that restoring a process is not equivalent to recovering data.
sources.relation_to_property: Backup/restore, state correctness and maintenance-induced failure.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Provider-authored account; nevertheless unusually detailed and falsifiable.

sources.exact_title: Preliminary Post Incident Review: Content Configuration Update Impacting the Falcon Sensor and the Windows Operating System
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: What happened, content validation and remediation sections
sources.claim_supported: Shows a shared update defect propagating through a broad homogeneous dependency despite existing test processes.
sources.relation_to_property: Correlated deployment risk, configuration binding and safe rollout.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Preliminary/provider-authored; full RCA may refine causal detail.

sources.exact_title: Helping Our Customers Through the CrowdStrike Outage
sources.claim_supported: Reports an estimated 8.5 million affected Windows devices and highlights broad consequence from concentrated critical-service dependency.
sources.relation_to_property: Field evidence for correlated infrastructure and supplier dependency.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Estimate is contemporary and not a complete independent impact assessment.

sources.exact_title: Implementing SLOs
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: User journeys, latency grades, freshness/durability, dependency modelling and error-budget policy sections
sources.claim_supported: Shows how SLOs can represent user-relevant measures, tails, degradation and dependency assumptions.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Google’s practice is not universal field proof and the chapter itself notes aggregation and independence problems.

sources.exact_title: Monitoring Distributed Systems
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Symptoms versus causes, four golden signals and alert design
sources.claim_supported: Frames monitoring around user-visible symptoms while retaining causal diagnostics.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The four signals are a useful translation, not a complete diagnostic-coverage argument.

sources.exact_title: Example Error Budget Policy
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Policy triggers, actions, stakeholder agreement and review
sources.claim_supported: Treats an error budget as a governed decision policy rather than a free licence for risky change.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Threshold and denominator choices remain gameable and user heterogeneity may be hidden.

sources.exact_title: What SRE Could Be
sources.claim_supported: Critiques boolean-ratio SLOs outside request/response services, poorly understood error-budget response, arbitrary thresholds and outage-duration aggregation.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Commentary rather than controlled evaluation, but mechanism-specific and grounded in practice.

sources.exact_title: Not All Minutes Are Equal: The Secret Behind SLO Adoption Failure
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Time-based versus event-based denominators and high-severity incident example
sources.claim_supported: Shows that SLO formula/denominator choice can materially change interpretation.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Conference case rather than peer-reviewed comparative study.

sources.exact_title: Chaos Engineering
sources.claim_supported: Defines controlled experimentation on distributed-system behaviour under failure conditions.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: An experiment supports only the tested hypothesis, fault, load, boundary and observation interval.

sources.exact_title: Principles of Chaos Engineering
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: Steady state, real-world events, production and automation principles
sources.claim_supported: Documents the intended hypothesis-driven rather than random-breakage form of chaos practice.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: A manifesto is advocacy, not independent effectiveness evidence.

sources.author_or_organisation: Joshua Owotogbe, Indika Kumara, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel and Damian Andrew Tamburri
sources.exact_title: Chaos Engineering: A Multi-Vocal Literature Review
sources.date_version_edition: 2025 online publication; ACM Computing Surveys 58(7), Article 164
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: 96 sources published January 2016–April 2024; findings, taxonomy and open challenges
sources.claim_supported: Synthesises practice and research while identifying evaluation, tooling and adoption gaps.
sources.relation_to_property: Current chaos-engineering state and evidence limits.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Multivocal sources vary in methodological quality.

sources.author_or_organisation: Nur Haninie Abd Wahab, Khairunnisa Hasikin, Khin Wee Lai, Kaijian Xia, Lulu Bei, Kai Huang and Xiang Wu
sources.exact_title: Systematic Review of Predictive Maintenance and Digital Twin Technologies: Challenges, Opportunities, and Best Practices
sources.exact_section_page_theorem_table_figure_: PeerJ Computer Science 10:e1943; PRISMA selection and 34 included articles from 2018–2023
sources.claim_supported: Shows rapid predictive-maintenance/digital-twin development alongside heterogeneous methods, sector coverage, cost and transfer challenges.
sources.relation_to_property: Current PdM evidence and transfer limits.
sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: The review does not establish universal superiority over simple preventive or run-to-failure policies.

sources.contrary_evidence_if_any: Production-system focus limits transfer to all missions and services.
